title: Second Largest Element in an Array without sorting
stepTitle: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
category: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
problemStatement: Find the second largest distinct element without sorting.
intuition: Track the two best distinct values at once. The subtlety is duplicates: a value equal to the largest must not become the second largest.

approaches.title: Brute: sort and scan back
approaches.idea: Sort, then walk from the end until a value differs from the last.

approaches.title: Optimal: two trackers in one pass
approaches.idea: largest and second; update second only when x < largest.
approaches.dryRun:
a=[1,2,4,7,7,5]
x=1 largest=1
x=2 largest=2 second=1
x=4 largest=4 second=2
x=7 largest=7 second=4
x=7 equal -> skipped
x=5 -> second=5
answer 5
approaches.whyWorks: The strict `x < largest` guard is exactly what makes duplicates of the max harmless.

edgeCases: All elements equal -> no second largest
commonMistakes: Using `x <= largest`, which lets a duplicate max become the second largest
patternRecognition: "Top-k for tiny k" -> k trackers in one pass beats sorting
followUps: Extend to the k-th largest without sorting
Second smallest in the same pass
What if the array can contain None/NaN?
interviewInsight: The duplicate-max case is the whole test. State it before you code.

related.title: Check if the array is sorted
